speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions. To understand the severity of your condition, have you had any recent trauma to your wrist, or is the pain arising spontaneously?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection (Gonorrhea).

The combination of a recent camping trip, self-resolving monoarticular knee pain, and now asymmetric wrist arthritis with fever and skin lesions in a sexually active male is highly suggestive of disseminated gonococcal infection. I will proceed to confirm this with a specific test.

REQUEST TEST: Gram_Stain_of_urine_and_Nucleic_Acid_Amplification_Test_(NAAT) for Neisseria_gonorrhoeae.
REQUEST IMAGES: Skin_lesions_close_up.
